activity.notes: Bhāskara II (Bhāskarācārya), a historical 12th-century Indian scholar, completed Siddhāntaśiromaṇi around 1150 (age 36) and produced Karaṇakutūhala dated to 1183. His mathematics spans arithmetic, algebra, quadratic indeterminate equations, and mathematical astronomy, and his works supported long-running Indian mathematics education. The existing India entity is only a broad geographic/civilizational affiliation for scholarship in medieval South Asia; it does NOT assert allegiance to or governance by the modern Indian Republic, or identify an undocumented medieval sovereign dynasty. His association with an astronomical observatory in Ujjain is documented, but the precise political ruler of his scholarly activity is not inferred here. End year 1183 marks a datable work, not an exact death or retirement date.
